subject: MedByte — Standard per-1M token IO rates & supported models
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@medbyte.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medbyte.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: per-1M token IO rates + model roster

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Were evaluating Redwood for a chat-triage feature and need a concise baseline for hosted pricing to share with our execs and procurement. Two quick asks: 1) your standard per-1M token input/output pricing for hosted API (no custom commitments) across the common model families you serve, and 2) a short list of models that would be supported for a production chat workload (low-latency, multi-turn, KV-cache friendly).

For context: MedByte is a digital triage vendor; expected ramp is roughly 50M tokens/month in Q2, with a target of 200M/month within 6 months if everything looks good. Were evaluating latency SLOs (~200-400ms p50 on short chats) and we will be handling PHI; procurement will need SOC 2 docs but I can handle that separately. I attached our RFP excerpt and a token estimate workbook.

Can you send a short table (per-1M input, per-1M output) and the model names youd recommend for our use case? Also let us know if you offer volume discounts or commit-based pricing.

Thanks,
Samir Gupta
Head of Product, MedByte Health
Samir@medbyte.ai
(Attachment: MedByte_RFP_Q1_2028.pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@medbyte.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-1M token IO rates + model roster

Hi Samir  thanks for the context and the RFP. Happy to get you a short, shareable table. Two quick clarifying Qs so we can give the most relevant recommendations:

- Expected input/output split (rough percent input vs output tokens)?
- Any hard latency requirement at p95? You mentioned p50 200-400ms which helps.
- Will you need EU data residency or strictly US-hosted?

Initial guidance below (hosted API, on-demand/no commit):
- redwood-infer-7b: $0.60 per 1M input / $1.40 per 1M output — good latency/throughput balance for short chats
- rw-stable-13b: $1.10 per 1M input / $2.25 per 1M output — higher quality for longer context and fewer hallucinations
- redwood-xl-v1: $2.50 per 1M input / $4.50 per 1M output — best-in-class for complex instruction-following, higher cost
- gptj-6b-quant (open): $0.35 per 1M input / $0.80 per 1M output — lower cost option; may need more tuning for PHI-sensitive prompts

If you expect a heavy output-dominant workload (e.g., summarization generating long outputs) the output-side economics will matter more; if short assistant responses, the input token volume tends to dominate. For the ramp you mentioned, commit discounts typically kick in around multi-month minimums — I can outline a simple tiering in my next note.

If you can share the input/output split and whether SOC2 + US-only hosting are must-haves, Ill follow up with a compact ratecard PDF and a recommended model matrix for your SLA profile.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Evelyn@redwood.com
(Attachment referenced: MedByte_token_estimates.xlsx)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@medbyte.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@medbyte.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-1M token IO rates + model roster

Evelyn  thanks for the quick turnaround.

Answers:
- Expected split: ~35% input / 65% output (we generate fairly long triage summaries and next-step recommendations).
- Latency: p95 target is 700ms or under for majority of calls; p50 target remains ~250ms.
- Data residency: US-only for now. SOC 2 Type II is required for procurement.

Procurement asks for an official rate sheet and a short note on typical volume discounts and minimum commitment levels. Can you also flag any models that are restricted for PHI or that require Private deployment?

Appreciate it,
Samir
(Attachment: MedByte_token_estimates.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@medbyte.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, procurement@medbyte.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood hosted rate summary & discount pathways — MedByte

Samir / Team,

Appreciate the details. Im attaching a concise hosted ratecard PDF and an example commit discount table. High-level summary below (all per 1M tokens):

On-demand (no commit):
- redwood-infer-7b: Input $0.60 / Output $1.40
- rw-stable-13b: Input $1.10 / Output $2.25
- redwood-xl-v1: Input $2.50 / Output $4.50
- gptj-6b-quant (open): Input $0.35 / Output $0.80

Commit tiers (volume = billed tokens/month):
- 3-month pilot (commit 100M/month): 15% discount on hosted IO rates
- 12-month standard (commit 150M/month): 30% discount
- Enterprise reserved (commit 500M+/month): custom pricing + priority capacity

Notes and clarifications:
- Discounts apply to the token IO line items only; usage above committed quantity is billed at on-demand rates unless a burn-forward clause is added.
- Models that handle PHI securely at scale and require Private deployment: redwood-xl-v1 (for customers requiring air-gapped or strict data residency controls we recommend Redwood Private). The other hosted models are SOC 2 covered and can be used on-hosted with customer-level controls; we will provide a SOC 2 package and KMS options.
- We can provide a short SOW and a mutual action plan for procurement to review.

Ive attached: Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_2028Q1.pdf (rate table), SOW_initial.docx (SOW template). Happy to hop on a 30m call with procurement to walk through the contract redlines.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
(Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_2028Q1.pdf, SOW_initial.docx)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@medbyte.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medbyte.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted rate summary & discount pathways  MedByte next steps

Ben / Evelyn  thanks, thats exactly what procurement needed. A few quick next steps on our side:

1) Well run internal numbers against the 35/65 split and the 150M/month uplift target and come back with a preferred commit tier by EOD Monday.
2) Procurement has requested a one-page mutual action plan and a DocuSign-ready rate sheet + SOW. Can you send a DocuSign link or a staged agreement?
3) Well need the SOC2 package and the US-only hosting confirmation to attach to the purchase request.

If you can drop the one-pager + DocuSign envelope by Monday morning (PST), Ill fast-track with procurement. Thanks again  looking forward to getting a pilot started.

Samir Gupta
Head of Product, MedByte Health
samir@medbyte.ai
